title: Machine learning reveals two previously undetected phases in Rydberg-atom quantum-simulator data
summary: An interpretable hybrid unsupervised/supervised learning analysis of experimental snapshots from a programmable Rydberg-atom array mapped phase regions on a square lattice and identified signatures of two previously undetected phases: boundary-ordered and rhombic. The rhombic pattern had been predicted theoretically, so the result is its experimental-data signature rather than a wholly unanticipated theoretical phase; the boundary-ordered phase was revealed from edge correlations.
ai_technology: Hybrid-correlation convolutional neural network (Hybrid-CCNN) with PCA and clustering
organization: Harvard University; Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Cornell University; collaborators

evidence.tested: An interpretable hybrid unsupervised/supervised learning analysis of experimental snapshots from a programmable Rydberg-atom array mapped phase regions on a square lattice and identified signatures of two previously undetected phases: boundary-ordered and rhombic.
evidence.unknown: The study reanalyzes experimental quantum-simulator snapshots; the rhombic phase was previously predicted by theory, while the paper reports its finite-size experimental manifestation. The paper characterizes phases using data and numerical interpretation, not bulk material synthesis.
evidence.ai_role: Unsupervised clustering exposed phase regions in experimental snapshots; interpretable supervised correlator networks refined boundaries and identified edge and multi-point correlation motifs characteristic of the previously undetected boundary-ordered and rhombic regions.
